full_text:
This is the strategy guide that you will need to dominate in NFL best ball tournaments.

Before you start drafting all of your favorite players from all of your favorite teams, it’s best to understand the table rules.

Best ball is not like managed leagues, in which you make weekly start/sit decisions. Sharp fantasy football managers treat them as two entirely different games. In order to win the DK Best Ball Millionaire tournament ($25 buy-in), you’ll need to beat out over 940,000 other entries. Underdog’s Best Ball Mania VII has 672,336 entrants.

Starting the 37th-best WR every week in a managed league is a replacement-level player if you only have to start two WRs in your league. Having this WR37 on your roster isn’t particularly valuable, even if you drafted them at a steep discount or picked them up off of waivers. A team filled with slight ADP values is going to be around .500 in season-long leagues.

In seasonal leagues, the pool of players that actually matter on a weekly basis is extremely narrow. That’s especially true during the fantasy playoffs (Weeks 15-17) after all of the injury attrition sinks in across the NFL. We make up for our mistakes in managed leagues with timely waiver pickups, trades, and churning through backup running backs on your bench.

On the other hand, drafting a best ball team filled with players that moderately beat their ADP value is basically the entire point of the game. Each round is filled with landmines, and that’s especially true late. Drafting usable players – ADP beaters – in Rounds 12-16 is a huge win.

Let’s discuss the key trends, roster construction strategy tips, and conditional drafting rules that you will need to select high-quality rosters that score a ton of fantasy points.

__Scoring and Roster Requirements__
-----------------------------------

__Half PPR vs. Full PPR scoring__
---------------------------------

DraftKings scoring rewards wide receivers more so than Underdog. That’s because full-point per reception scoring produces more usable players on a weekly basis compared to Half-PPR.

The best example of this scoring difference in action is Ladd McConkey’s 2025 season.

McConkey was the WR37 in Half-PPR FPG last season. His 9.2 FPG was equivalent to the RB34 in Half-PPR scoring, David Montgomery.

McConkey’s 11.7 DK FPG was more valuable, however. His production was equivalent to the RB28 in PPR, outscoring Ken Walker.

Among all players that scored 100 or more DraftKings FP over the last two seasons, RBs out-scored the WRs by 1.4 FPG on average.

#### DraftKings positional scoring by week (2024-25 seasons)

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/e2c81eb63033c17abbae4c68e0c3846d920b2028)

This scoring gap widens in Half-PPR formats.

Over the last two seasons, nearly 200 RB/WR have scored at least 100 Half-PPR points in a single season. (To be precise, there are 199 instances).

Among these players, the RBs outscored the WRs by 2 Half-PPR fantasy points per game on average.

#### Half-PPR positional scoring by week (2024-25 seasons)

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/63fee73d43d7b9b51710a138ef4bbe64d5181efe)

Let’s zoom all the way out here before we move on.

Even in another dominant season for running backs, eight of the top-15 scoring players by DraftKings FPG were receivers in 2025.

Conversely, running backs dominated in Half-PPR scoring formats. 10 of the top-15 scoring players in FPG were runners. The only five wide receivers that managed to crack the top-15 were Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Ja’Marr Chase, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Rashee Rice.

Fantasy football has always been ruled by one key principle: Running backs are more valuable than wide receivers; the degree to which this is true just varies by season.

__Will WR Scoring Rebound?__
----------------------------

Passing was at an historic low last year. Yards per game league-wide hit a low not seen since 2006. The pass-friendly 2010s are long gone, replaced by wholesale changes in the way defenses are constructed. EDGE rushers are leaner and more athletic. Coverage has skewed more zone-heavy, rewarding creative passing attacks that can pick holes in these zones and receivers that are fast and elusive after the catch.

Two-high safety coverage has one drawback – removing a defender from the box can leave you vulnerable on the ground. Offenses are responding by playing heavier personnel. Extra offensive linemen and tight ends have replaced 3-WR sets.

There are reasons to be optimistic, though.

Only 16 passers eclipsed 225 passing yards per game last season. Our projections have 20 passers exceeding 225 YPG this year.

Bad luck with injuries has been a running theme at quarterback and receiver the last two seasons.

Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, Lamar Jackson, Jayden Daniels, and Daniel Jones are all returning from injury. Brock Purdy only appeared in nine games in 2025. Baker Mayfield struggled through multiple injuries.

Wide receiver scoring has been tamped down by changes in NFL philosophy and a recent run of bad injury luck. As Ryan Heath [noted](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2025/ryan-heaths-fantasy-football-takeaways#/), the top-30 WRs in last year’s average draft position all played in their lowest percentage of possible games (79%) in the last decade. This was eight percentage points lower than average (87%).

We’ve also had [two rough years for QB injuries](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2012277935646945790/photo/1?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2012277935646945790%7Ctwgr%5E3b1c962d1b4156e2fec0c022b7b4dfb57f99fe46%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fantasypoints.com%2Fnfl%2Farticles%2Fseason%2F2025%2Fryan-heaths-fantasy-football-takeaways%2F) in 2023 and 2025, with the top passers in ADP only playing 74% and 78% of possible games, respectively, per Heath’s analysis.

Trying to predict injuries is a fool’s errand. The only thing we can really do is analyze the players that have an outsized or discounted injury risk relative to their ADP.

However, we can be extremely confident that returning to base injury rates will naturally elevate passing attacks.

Running backs are the most important position to get right in fantasy football. That has always been the case, and the importance has only been heightened with the NFL’s recent changes. The markets have responded.

__ADP Trends__
--------------

The running back market is running hotter than ever. The top-15 RBs in average draft position are being selected 7.6 overall picks earlier compared to 2022-25.

The market momentum continues the further we get down the board.

The RB20 is being selected 17.1 overall picks earlier than the previous four-year average!

#### Underdog RB ADP – Last 5 Years

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/cc9444926f9b71da2e2e385fd161fd6b45066257)

With the market pendulum shifting towards running backs, the entire WR market gets cheaper beyond WR35 in ADP. This trend starts around 70 overall and doesn’t abate. I’ve pointed that out on the chart below.

#### Underdog WR ADP – Last 5 Years

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/61b5ccf8d0a2c08b6d8345b290e3ea4fdf3b1bac)

For example, the WR50 is going off the board about nine overall picks later than usual.

This coincides with drafters taking quarterbacks earlier than normal, starting around QB10, and the QB market accelerates further past 100 overall.

\> All of this reinforces the importance of nailing your RB-RB starts in Rounds 1-2, because WRs are on sale. Round 3-5 is stocked with a lot of talented receivers.

#### Underdog QB ADP – Last 5 Years

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/7eee06b94f12f4055ed17b6c854fdcdaa7e97b07)

The pocket where drafters take their QB2 and QB3 – from QB18-QB30 in positional ADP – became more expensive in 2025, and that trend has continued in 2026.

The position has continued to compress upwards, and this is somewhat due to scarcity. There is high uncertainty about the playing time for the Falcons, Browns, and Raiders quarterbacks and moderate uncertainty about the Cardinals.

It’s always best to keep in mind that quarterback ADP in best ball formats is largely driven by stacks. This slightly tighter ADP environment at QB also means that you will have a lower chance of a potential value falling way past their typical cost, at least relative to previous seasons.

This season’s TE market closely tracks 2025 drafts until the TE18-TE30 pocket. Drafters are pushing up their TE2-3 earlier than ever.

#### Underdog TE ADP – Last 5 Years

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/0893cb87d441c60d9822c1e6f53d428ec7ae1121)

The wide receiver market isn’t just being squeezed by running backs. The market is also forcing QB and TE up in priority, particularly in the late rounds starting around 100 overall.

__Adapting to the Changing Market__
-----------------------------------

I pulled the last five years of individual advance rate for every drafted player on Underdog and binned them by ADP. For example, any team with Jonathan Taylor (20.9 ADP) last season had a 48.8% advance rate to the Week 15 playoff round.

I also binned each drafted team’s total points scored to give us another layer of context.

This table below shows that the Underdog teams that were in the 50th percentile (or higher) in total points scored in an individual season simply drafted their running backs “better” than the bottom-50% in the premium rounds.

Take a look at the scoring gap in the rightmost column:

#### Average Team Points Scored by Round (1-6) – RB vs. WR

 Position Top 50% avg TeamPts Bottom 50% avg TeamPts Gap RB 1,340 1,229 +112 WR 1,288 1,283 +6 

This doesn’t mean that wide receivers don’t move the needle in the early rounds. Just over half of all 90th percentile scores (>24 FP) at wide receiver [will come from players selected in the first three rounds of drafts](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2025/underdog-best-ball-draft-guide#/).

Running backs have an outsized effect on your team’s ceiling outcomes in Rounds 1-6. Drafting well at wide receiver early just doesn’t have the same order of magnitude.

Over the last five seasons, RBs have outperformed the WRs in Round 2 and 3 by their advance rate to the Week 15 playoff round. This recent ADP shift – pushing running backs over wide receivers – is efficient.

However, wide receivers have outperformed the running backs by a wide margin in Rounds 4 and 5:

#### Advance Rates by Round (1-6) – RB vs. WR

Selecting WRs in the 37-60 overall range has historically been the strongest pocket for value – the receivers outperformed the runners by 3.3-3.4%, on average. This doesn’t mean that you should avoid RBs entirely within Rounds 4 and 5, but it’s pretty clear that’s the dead zone for the position.

An outsized amount of “league-winning” receivers are typically found in Round 4.

There are 12 WRs and 8 RBs selected between Rounds 4-5 in drafts currently.

If you want to counter the field, drafting WRs heavily in Rounds 4-5 is the move. These receivers are cheaper than normal, and the opportunity cost is at running back only. Take a look at the graphs in the section above again – the QB and TE market prior to 100 overall hasn’t changed.

\> DraftKings hasn’t released pick-by-pick data, so this logic can’t be directly applied 1-for-1. Recall that Underdog’s Half-PPR scoring rewards running backs more. The interpositional value equation changes a bit on DraftKings because full-PPR scoring helps narrow the scoring gap between RB and WR. I’d be cautious about getting caught up in positional runs where the draft room chases RB on DraftKings, especially in Rounds 4-6.

__Roster Construction and Conditional Drafting Rules__
------------------------------------------------------

If we gave every person in your 12-team draft the same skill level while ignoring injuries and randomness, then everyone’s equal chances of advancing as a top-2 scoring team to the playoff round in Week 15 is 16.67% (two out of 12). Two teams advance out of 12 in both DraftKings and Underdog’s flagship contests.

To measure the advance rate for these positional strategies, we can do so by comparing your baseline odds (16.67%) against the data for the varying roster construction strategies (i.e. 2-QB vs. 3-QB builds).

By measuring advance rate over or under expected – where 16.7% is perfectly average – we will have a better grasp on the strategies that give us the biggest edge in building rosters.

+ __AROE__ = Advance Rate Over Expectation (to Week 15 playoffs)

+ __ARUE__ = Advance Rate Under Expectation

#### Quarterbacks

The field continues to draft more best ball teams with 3 quarterbacks on Underdog:

{{PAYWALL}} ![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/f36776d3bd643093022d109af0410446206d5ecb)

And for good reason!

Drafting three passers on one team has elevated your chances of advancing to the playoffs in three straight seasons, and these teams produced a five-year best +1.4% AROE in 2025. Conversely, 2-QB teams have performed below expectation in each of the last three years by -0.6% on average.

The late-round QB strategy has dominated in best ball, likely aided by two rough seasons for injuries. Quantity can replace quality during lean scoring weeks. Avoiding zeros at quarterback is key. Waiting until Round 9 or later to draft your QB1 and selecting three total QBs has produced a +2.2% AROE over the last three years.

Team stacks play a component in this data as well. When a quarterback has a spiked week, their WR1 (by target share) sees a 53% higher chance of an equal spiked scoring week.

On DraftKings, the extra two rounds (20 total) significantly decreases the opportunity cost of rostering 3-QBs. I’d recommend taking 3-QB on almost every team in any best ball format with 20 rounds.

We will see the 3-QB strategy surpass 2-QB in popularity for the first time on Underdog this season.

#### Running Backs

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/c394b298544a414ef6ff7fee66e34ba00a0dafdb)

Over the last five years, the only strategy that has posted a positive advance rate in every season is 5-RB builds. 2024 and 2025 have been dominant in that regard.

On Underdog, 5-RB is clearly optimal. 6-RB teams are the second-most popular build behind 5-RB.

Selecting 5-RB total and at least two RBs in Rounds 1-4 has produced a ridiculous +7.1% AROE across the last two seasons. That’s mainly driven by __Jonathan Taylor__ (2025) and __Saquon Barkley__ (2024) carrying teams as second-round picks.

\> Because 5-RB is optimal, it places the utmost importance on nailing the correct RBs in the first 36 picks. The vast majority of league-winning RBs are selected in Rounds 1-3. Two stud RBs and then attacking WR in Rounds 4-5 is my preferred strategy.

The RB renaissance has also created an avenue to build some high-upside 4-RB teams, producing a small sample high AROE in back-to-back seasons. Just 5-7% of drafters have risked having just 4-RBs over the last two seasons, respectively.

#### Wide Receivers

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/9dc5fdeeb038914a2e8918f5ac5a7286b2eb8c06)

Over the last five seasons, 77% of the field has drafted between 7- and 8-WR on Underdog. Both strategies have near equal success.

The vast majority of your rosters should have 7-8 WR on Underdog and between 8-9 WR on DraftKings because 3-TE is optimal.

#### Tight Ends

Drafting 3-TE has provided a positive advance rate in five straight seasons, with each of the last two years sitting at +2% AROE.

Stopping at 2-TE has basically only made sense if you drafted Trey McBride in 2024 or 2025.

That’s because 50 of the top-70 TEs by regular season advance rate were drafted at 125 overall or later over the last five years. That’s 71%.

Only 4-of-15 TEs drafted in Rounds 1-4 have produced a positive advance rate in this same timeframe. It generally pays to be patient and hunt for value later at tight end.

Trey McBride, Brock Bowers, and Colston Loveland are aiming to break that trend this year.

If you have zero TE rostered after Round 9, it’s always best to end your draft with 3-TE total. Three-TE teams have produced a +2.2% AROE compared to 2-TE in this scenario.

__Underdog Ideal Roster Construction__
--------------------------------------

+ QB: 2-3

+ RB: 5
+ WR: 7-8
+ TE: 3

__DraftKings Ideal Roster Construction__
----------------------------------------

+ QB: 3

+ RB: 5-6
+ WR: 8-9
+ TE: 3

__Stacking Guide__
------------------

Drafting players from the same team is heavily correlated with your success in best ball leagues, especially in large-field tournaments. Selecting the “right” team stack can make up for a lot of mistakes either from an individual player standpoint or a roster construction standpoint.

The total number of stacked players from the same team on your best ball roster – regardless of position – has a positive relationship with the amount of regular season points your team scored. 24.7% of regular season fantasy scoring variance (measured by RSQ) is explained by the number of stacked players rostered. This means that your stacks alone will explain about a quarter of your team’s total fantasy points scored.

The top quarterbacks in regular season advance rate often carry at least two of their teammates with them.

Of the 46 quarterbacks with an advance rate at least 2% above average over the last five seasons, 43 QBs had at least two teammates (RB, WR, or TE) who also posted above-average individual advance rates. That’s 93.5%.

On average, these QBs had 2.9 teammates with an above-average advance rate. 20 of these 46 (43.5%) quarterbacks supported a full-team stack – at least one RB, WR, and TE with an advance rate of 16.8% or higher.

Let’s take a top-down approach to the league’s best offenses entering 2026.

First, we’ll use our site projections (PPR) to determine which offenses have the best outlook.

Using the NFL lookahead spreads and totals, we can infer how many points per game each offense will score across the season.

__Projected Top-5 Offenses__
----------------------------

#### Detroit Lions

The Lions are the top offense in our projections, and they are tied for second in implied points per game (26.1). By projected win totals, they also have the NFL’s easiest strength of schedule.

The team outlook for __Jahmyr Gibbs__ is just way better than it is for __Bijan Robinson__ (Falcons 23rd in projected FP | 25th implied PPG), if you’re trying to split a tie. Detroit remained very run-heavy (-7% PROE) inside-the-10 last year even when compared to OC Ben Johnson’s final season (-9%) in 2024, giving Gibbs the ceiling to score 18-20 touchdowns.

__Jared Goff__ is one of the best QB values (QB16 ADP) and someone I’m targeting. Goff is a strong technical value as the QB10 in FPG, and he’s shown elite efficiency on an EPA/DB basis (+0.22, third-best) over the last two years. Only Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson have been better on a per dropback basis. Goff is set up as one of the highest-potential advance-rate QBs at his 110 overall ADP.

__Amon-Ra St. Brown__ has at least 100 receptions and has averaged 80.9 yards per game over his last four campaigns. In their nine games together before __Sam LaPorta__ missed Weeks 11- 18 with an injury, St. Brown led the Lions with a monster 39% first-read target share over LaPorta (17%) and __Jameson Williams__ (16%). After Gibbs, Robinson, Chase, Nacua, and McCaffrey are drafted – there’s not a single player with a higher floor than St. Brown.

#### Dallas Cowboys

__Dak Prescott__ has attempted at least 590 passes and thrown for at least 30 TDs in each of his last three full seasons with 16 or more games, finishing as fantasy’s QB3, QB6, and QB7. He’s correctly priced as the QB7 on both DraftKings and Underdog.

Prescott is good enough to support two top-12 fantasy WRs again, and I feel strongly that __CeeDee Lamb__ has a higher floor than __Justin Jefferson__ because of QB play. Lamb’s volume was still very good last year. Lamb saw more first-read targets (32%) and had a significantly more valuable role (18.3 XFP/G) than __George Pickens__ (26% FR TS | 13.1 XFP/G) in their 12 full games together last season. Lamb missed Weeks 3-6 with an ankle injury.

__Javonte Williams__ is priced up as a Round 3-4 turn pick, and we’ve got him ranked as a better value on Underdog (+6 spots overall) than on DraftKings (+2). Still only 26 years old, Williams is now four years removed from his knee injury in 2022. Williams averaged 2.9 yards after contact per carry last year, nearly matching his elite rookie season (3.2 YACO/attempt). Maybe he doesn’t offer huge upside on passing downs, but the goal-line role is super valuable in this offense. Williams ranked RB9 in share of carries inside-the-5 and was RB7 in expected Rush TDs last year.

#### Los Angeles Rams

The 2025 Rams were one of the most valuable team stacks over the last five fantasy football seasons, especially after the __Matthew Stafford__ (back) fear, uncertainty, and doubt from last August.

Stafford is the reigning MVP, but the markets (QB14 ADP) are correctly baking in regression for this offense. Sure, his lofty 7.7% TD is bound to fall back down closer to his base rate with the Rams (5.6% TD). Even with this baked in, Stafford still comes out of the projections (QB13) favorably.

In their 13 full games together, __Puka Nacua__ dominated targets (29% share) over __Davante Adams__ (23%). Los Angeles is expected to score -3.9 fewer points per game this season, which would impact Adams more than Nacua. The majority of Adams’ fantasy value was driven by touchdowns last year as he earned a ridiculous 24 end-zone targets to Nacua’s three.

__Kyren Williams__’ stranglehold on goal-line work diminished last season as he and __Blake Corum__ split carries inside-the-5 by a 52% to 38% margin. With limited passing-down upside to begin with – HC __Sean McVay__ rarely designs pass plays to his RBs – Williams (30-32 overall ADP, RB15) is one of the most overvalued players in the first 3 rounds of drafts. The Rams rank 31st, 31st, and 32nd in RB receptions over the last three seasons.

#### Cincinnati Bengals

The Bengals are fourth in projections and tied for second in implied PPG. Cincinnati also has the second-easiest strength of schedule.

This offense will go as far as __Joe Burrow__ takes them. Cincinnati leads the league in EPA/DB (+0.24) when Burrow is on the field since 2022, and they fall to 14th (+0.05) without him.

__Ja’Marr Chase__ vs. __Puka Nacua__ is very close. In my opinion, Chase just has slightly more upside attached to a fully healthy Burrow. The volume is incredible in this passing offense. The Bengals lead the NFL in pass rate (66%) since 2022 as Burrow (37.7) leads all passers in attempts per game. Burrow ranks 1st (2025), 1st, (‘24) 8th (‘23), and 2nd (‘22) in catchable throw rate in this span.

Chase averages a ridiculous 22.6 PPR FPG per Burrow start (2024-25), which makes him WR1 over Nacua (21.6).

By extension, __Tee Higgins__ (17.5 PPR FPG – WR5) has feasted over the last two seasons when Burrow is on the field. As the WR17 in ADP on Underdog, Higgins is the most undervalued WR on the board in the top-36 picks.

Based on volume (RB6 in expected FPG since 2024), __Chase Brown__ (RB10) is at least a little undervalued. This offense is just so pass-heavy inside-the-10 (+12% PROE – 2024-25) that it caps Brown’s touchdown upside a bit.

#### Buffalo Bills

__Josh Allen__ is fantasy gold, finishing as the QB1 in FPG in four out of the last five seasons. He ranks second in pass TD and fourth in rush TD among all players since 2021.

__D.J. Moore__’s efficiency has declined in three straight seasons (2.47 YPRR > 1.53 > 1.33), but I’m leaving the light on that Allen can elevate Moore for a season. Allen is QB3 in EPA/DB (scrambles removed) over the last two years, trailing only Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson. __Stefon Diggs__ is a better receiver than Moore, but he’s an example of Moore’s bull case. Three out of Diggs’ 4 best seasons in yards per game were attached to Allen.

Moore has earned at least 30% of his team’s first-read targets in four out of the last 5 seasons, with last year (18%) being the lone exception. __Khalil Shakir__’s career-high is 25% FR. __Dalton Kincaid__ has never topped a 21% first-read target share. Kincaid simply needs to play a larger role in the offense to become a difference-maker in fantasy. He ranks TE37 (2025), TE27 (‘24), and TE14 (‘23) in route share over his career.

__James Cook__ is a key target at the end of Round 1 thanks to his locked-in TD upside attached to Allen. The Lions lead the NFL in plays inside the 10 over the last two seasons (210) but only they and the Rams (199) are ahead of the Bills (198). Cook has untapped upside as a receiver in the screen game, should HC __Joe Brady__ finally utilize him more in that department. Just 6% of Cook’s targets were “designed” plays, which is 44th-of-45 RBs since 2024.

__Top-12 Offenses__
-------------------

\> You will notice that the sixth-best offense (Kansas City) and 21st-best (Houston) are separated by less than 100 total FP. Let’s break down the key differences between each team outlook and try to identify potential breakout attacks.

#### Baltimore Ravens

The Ravens are fifth in implied points per game with __Lamar Jackson__ back healthy after missing time last year with a hamstring injury. In case you need a reminder, Jackson is one of the most efficient passers in football. He ranks QB2 in YPA (8.4) and QB1 in Pass TD% (7%) since 2023. This is the cheapest price (56 overall) that we’ve seen for Lamar since 2021 (54 overall ADP).

This offense will be very consolidated.

Baltimore’s strong team outlook means that __Derrick Henry__’s high-scoring equity is locked in. He leads all RBs in rushing TDs (32) scored since joining the Ravens. Baltimore has the fifth-easiest strength of schedule entering 2026.

__Zay Flowers__ became the first WR to finish top-15 in FPG in Lamar’s career last year, and he’s poised for career-best volume to repeat. Flowers saw elite target volume (27% share – WR7) and maintained excellent efficiency (2.61 YPRR – WR6) on his looks last season.

__Mark Andrews__ (TE15 ADP) is a phenomenal value on DraftKings. Even as a part-time player, Andrews is TE2 in expected receiving TDs over the last two seasons, just behind George Kittle. The Ravens have no choice but to play Andrews more often with Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar no longer on the roster. Andrews has the potential to play on 81% of pass downs again, just like in 2021-22.

#### San Francisco 49ers

HC __Kyle Shanahan__ was ranked as the best playcaller in the NFL by eight opposing defensive coordinators, according to this [excellent piece](https://x.com/FB_FilmAnalysis/status/2082437549109526898?s=20) by *The Athletic’s* Ted Nguyen. No matter the injuries or which QB is under center, the 49ers offense has consistently put up points. The 49ers have ranked 3rd, 12th, 2nd, and 8th in possessions that ended in a FG or TD over the last four seasons.

Once again, __Brock Purdy__ (ADP QB12) is underrated. Since 2023, Purdy has been fantasy's QB5 in FPG (19.5) by a hair over Joe Burrow (19.4). In this span, Purdy leads all QBs in EPA/DB and YPA. There is a chance that Purdy can push for 35-38 TDs on the high end range of outcomes after he’s finished top-2 in Pass TD% in two out of the last 3 years.

T __Trent Williams__ returning for one more year is huge for the 49ers' outlook.

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/9fb42bc0a5b5c390ba3ec13b6befcf6eb92146ba)

\> Fantasy Points Data

The 49ers are the most efficient offense in football with Williams on the field (+0.13 EPA/Play), but drop to 17th when he’s out.

Look at how much better the run game is with Williams, too. By extension, this offensive environment and insane passing down usage for __Christian McCaffrey__ insulates a lot of any potential age-related dropoff in skill.

__Mike Evans__ is still playing at a very high level, earning a target on 28% of his routes in 2025 (WR8) and 2024 (WR11). My concern about Evans’ target share dipping in San Francisco has been alleviated because of __Ricky Pearsall__’s lingering knee injury and veteran __Christian Kirk__ (calf) missing the start of training camp. Pearsall could miss a big chunk of the season, so Evans will be relied on heavily. It’s just his own injury issues (two hamstring strains, broken collarbone) that have tamped down some enthusiasm at Evans’ ADP. He’s been available to play just 22 games over the last two seasons.

__George Kittle__ has finished as a top-3 TE in FPG in four out of the last five seasons. He stands to benefit from Pearsall missing 2026, too. Kittle has a back-weighted projection because you know he’ll likely contribute little in September. This is easy to overcome in best ball because you should be building 3-TE teams anyway.

#### Chicago Bears

I was on the Bears as the breakout best ball team stack last season, and that worked fairly well. Chicago was one of 7 offenses that supported a full team stack (at least one QB, RB, WR, and TE with a positive advance rate).

The prices have come way up on __Caleb Williams__, __Luther Burden__, and __Colston Loveland__.

__Rome Odunze__ was producing as a top-12 fantasy WR before his foot injury last season, then his November-December slowdown coincided with __Luther Burden__ and __Colston Loveland__ getting more involved in the offense. It will be very hard for all 3 of the Bears pass catchers to pay off at their elevated ADP, but at least one player will likely be a strong value. Loveland is my favorite bet after he closed his rookie campaign with 14.5 PPR FPG (TE5) over his final 12 contests (including playoffs).

#### Kansas City Chiefs

The Chiefs have been a disappointing offense since 2023. They’ve finished outside of the top-8 scoring teams in three-straight seasons – ranking 10th (twice) and 15th (last year) in scoring drives.

Even though he’s expected to be ready by Week 1, we have to expect a dip in __Patrick Mahomes__’ scrambling ability after his knee injury. Mahomes averaged a career-high 30 rush YPG and TDs (5) in 2025, which really helped buoy his fantasy value. The passing efficiency has flatlined over the last three years (4.5% TD, 7.0 YPA) compared to his first 5 seasons (6.5% TD, 8.1 YPA). Mahomes is our projected QB13 and is overpriced at his QB11 ADP.

I don’t see the upside case for __Travis Kelce__ (ADP TE10). Over his last 11 full games with __Rashee Rice__ on the field for more than 5 snaps, Kelce has earned just 16.8% (TE10) of the Chiefs' targets. It’s translated into low-end TE1 volume (5.9 TGT/G – TE9).

We’re projecting the Chiefs' pass rate to drop by 2-3%, and that bodes very well for __Ken Walker__’s outlook. This backfield has underperformed their expected TD by the second-widest margin over the last two years, a trend that Walker could flip. Kansas City has scored a TD on just 25% of inside-the-10 carries (sixth-lowest rate) while Walker has been a good but not great goal-line RB (38% TD inside-10). Kansas City reportedly thinks there is untapped potential for Walker in the passing game, per [*ESPN*](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49098765/2026-kansas-city-chiefs-training-camp-preview)[’s Nate Taylor](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49098765/2026-kansas-city-chiefs-training-camp-preview).

#### Green Bay Packers

The Packers are projected to outscore the Chiefs and Bears by a razor-thin margin (0.4 PPG).

__Josh Jacobs__ is currently being investigated for a domestic violence case, and the NFL won’t decide on any suspension until the legal process plays out. Jacobs' fantasy upside is entirely tied to scoring at the goal-line. Only Derrick Henry (84%) had a higher share of his carries inside-the-5 last season than Jacobs (83%).

My favorite way to build around the Packers is through __Jordan Love__ and the passing attack. Love is QB7 in FP/DB (0.51) over the last two seasons, just slightly behind Burrow and Purdy (0.52). He also ranks QB7 in TD% (5.6%). He looks undervalued at his consensus QB18 ADP.

__Christian Watson__ just finished as the WR18 by FPG and has underrated upside in Round 5 at his WR28 ADP. Watson has shown elite efficiency with 2.67 YPRR (WR4) and 2.65 YPRR (WR8) in his last two seasons. There is a lot of TD equity available here. New Patriots WR __Romeo Doubs__ (9) led the team in end-zone targets last year, followed by Watson (5).

There is a small injury discount on __Tucker Kraft__ (TE4 in FPG last year) across the best ball markets (TE5 ADP). He makes a ton of sense as a part of 3-TE teams.

Even though I am enthusiastic about the Packers offense, __Matthew Golden__ looks like a Ponzi scheme. He was sixth on the team in targets per route run (0.17) as a rookie, and he was not a target-earner in college.

#### New England Patriots

The Patriots are the biggest regression candidates on offense year-over-year (implied for -5 fewer PPG). We’re projecting that __Drake Maye__’s TD% will drop modestly from 6.3% to 5.5%. He can overcome a dip in efficiency with passing volume.

Patriots OC __Josh McDaniels__ turned the keys over to his young quarterback last season, installing the fifth-most pass-heavy offense (+5.4% over expectation). __A.J. Brown__ is set for a boost to his target upside, at least relative to his former team. Philadelphia never ranked higher than 11th in pass rate over expectation in each of the last four seasons.

Brown’s target competition in New England is also significantly weaker than it was in Philadelphia. Brown is WR4 in first-read target share (36%) over the last two combined seasons while playing with __DeVonta Smith__ (31% – WR11) and __Dallas Goedert__ (22% – TE6). Brown is certainly going to be the alpha lined up next to moderate target-earners like __Romeo Doubs__ (22% first-read target share) and __Hunter Henry__ (19%).

The largest regression impact on the Patriots is definitely in the backfield. This is not baked into __TreVeyon Henderson__’s price in Round 5. __Rhamondre Stevenson__ and Henderson played in 17 games together, including the postseason. Stevenson (64%) played more snaps than Henderson (34%), had a higher share of carries (182 to 145), and he doubled up Henderson in routes (51% to 26%).

New England’s backfield produced the second-most expected TDs (20) last season, a figure we’re projecting to decline by -36%.

#### Seattle Seahawks

Seattle finished third in PPG last season, and yet __Sam Darnold__ was still just a middling QB2 in fantasy football. He was QB23 by FPG. The Seahawks backfield was super valuable, but split between two players.

__Jadarian Price__ is a rare rookie running back with a front-weighted projection. __Zach Charbonnet__ had ACL surgery on February 20, putting his return timeline until after Halloween. This was the most valuable backfield by expected FPG (18.1) just last year. Even with some regression baked into the offense, Price has underrated upside. He has a chance to run away with this backfield in September while Charbonnet is rehabbing.

__Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ vs. Amon-Ra St. Brown for WR4 is a coin flip decision. Our projections have them very close, but we slightly prefer the Lions' pass volume (138 targets for St. Brown and 131 for Smith-Njigba). I’m splitting the tie between the quality of offense. Seattle ranks 9th in implied PPG and 14th in projected FP, while Detroit is a top-2 projected attack.

__Breakout and Bounceback Offenses__
------------------------------------

#### Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jaguars are our breakout offense, ranking seventh in projected team fantasy points. HC __Liam Coen__ has established himself as a top-5 playcaller after coaching the Buccaneers to the fourth-most TD drives in 2024 and then the Jaguars to the 8th-most TD/possession last season. __Trevor Lawrence__ needed two months to get acclimated to the new offense, and then he closed out the season 5th in EPA/DB (+0.17) in Weeks 9-18 after the bye.

Stacking this team is very easy with __Bhayshul Tuten__ in Round 5 and then __Trevor Lawrence__ in Round 8.

It was across different sample sizes of carries (260 vs. 83), but Tuten actually bested Travis Etienne in yards after contact per carry, missed tackles forced per carry, and success rate according to our Fantasy Points Data. Etienne’s departure opens up a role worth 14.6 expected PPR FPG (RB12).

__Jakobi Meyers__ is the most mispriced receiver (ADP WR48) in best ball. Meyers was WR24 in FPG in eight games with 65% or more of snaps after joining the Jaguars. He slightly underperformed based on his role (WR16 in XFP/G) after he led the Jaguars WR group in target share and first-reads. __Brian Thomas__ and __Parker Washington__ have both shown more upside, but Meyers is the perfect example of a best ball ADP beater (that has little upside beyond being a WR3 in managed leagues).

#### Los Angeles Chargers

The Chargers are the second breakout offense as the ninth-best attack in projected FP. This high confidence projection bodes well for __Justin Herbert__ (QB9 ADP) stacks.

It was only in nine contests played, but __Omarion Hampton__ (15.1 FPG) outscored Ashton Jeanty (14.5) on a per-game basis last season. Hampton has huge upside as the potential bell cow of this offense. As a rookie, he played on 78% of the Chargers' snaps (RB7) in his first four games prior to injuring his ankle in Week 5. New OC __Mike McDaniel__’s Dolphins backfields have finished seventh, seventh, and first in team RB PPR points scored across the last three seasons.

Jeanty and Hampton’s ADP should be closer – I straight up prefer Hampton. Los Angeles is implied for 4.4 more PPG and 4 more wins than Las Vegas.

#### Philadelphia Eagles

The Eagles are a top-5 offense whenever Lane Johnson is on the field by EPA/Play over the last two seasons.

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/1daac8cf6bf696e783b7cd0261fb5a4b21466325/fe3c5b4eda38434b5d1ac18ad297d1a0f083c25e)

\> Fantasy Points Data

This entire Eagles offense should bounce back with Johnson healthy and a new playcaller in town. This is the cheapest ADP (70-75 overall) that __Jalen Hurts__ has had since 2021.

__Saquon Barkley__ fell off last season because his offensive line struggled to stay healthy and stagnant playcalling kept stalling out drives. Barkley was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage on 43% of his runs last season, way up from 35% in 2025.

This is __DeVonta Smith__’s big chance to prove that he’s an alpha. Over the past two seasons, Smith has played in four games without Brown, in which he averaged 31% more targets per game (6.3 T/G with Brown vs. 8.3 T/G without) and 15% more expected fantasy points per game (12.8 XFP/G with Brown vs. 14.7 XFP/G without). By volume alone, this would upgrade Smith from a WR2 to more of a low-end WR1.

__Dallas Goedert__ has seen a similar boost to his volume when Brown is off the field. Goedert has earned 28% more targets per game and averaged 34% more XFP per game in five contests without Brown over the last two seasons. As far as value goes, Goedert (TE15 ADP) is the safest bet within this passing offense. Goedert has finished top-12 by PPR FPG in four-straight seasons, two of which were top-8 campaigns.

#### Tampa Bay Buccaneers

__Baker Mayfield__ is one of the most undervalued players in best ball after he’s finished QB6 in FPG (19.7) over the last two years, just nudging out QB7 Brock Purdy and QB8 Patrick Mahomes by one-tenth of a point. Ryan Heath [views](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact) OC __Zac Robinson__ as a huge upgrade, one that could elevate this passing attack. Mayfield is QB19 in ADP.

__Emeka Egbuka__ leads off a long, flat tier of WR as an exciting breakout candidate. Egbuka suffered most from Mayfield playing through a shoulder injury last season. Just two years ago, Mayfield was QB3 in catchable throw rate (81%). Just 64% of Egbuka’s targets were catchable last season, which was the fifth-lowest rate among 86 WR.

__Jalen McMillan__ (WR60 ADP) is a strong value and has some underrated upside. Over his last 10 games played, McMillan has averaged 13.4 PPR FPG. He led the Buccaneers in YPRR last season, albeit on a small sample of routes (4 games).

#### Denver Broncos

The Broncos have a top-3 offensive line and top-3 defense – this team is primed to be able to run the ball well and be in plenty of good game-scripts. One of __RJ Harvey__ (RB31 ADP), __J.K. Dobbins__ (RB36), or __Jonah Coleman__ (RB48) needs to be a part of your draft plan. There is a ton of value here. Denver ranks 7th, 4th, and 1st in RB receptions over the last three seasons, and Dobbins was a solid fantasy RB2 as the Broncos' early-down runner last season. Harvey led all RBs in XFP/RR last season (0.50) over McCaffrey (0.48), Gibbs (0.44), and Achane (0.43).

__Bo Nix__ is QB9 in FPG over the last two seasons and is a good value (QB15-16 ADP) in the best ball markets. Adding __Jaylen Waddle__ will help spike Nix’s middling passing efficiency (QB17 in FP/DB).

__Potential Top-16 Offenses__
-----------------------------

\> Ranked 17-23rd.

#### Indianapolis Colts

The Colts scare me. Indianapolis is the third-largest regression candidate on offense, implied to score -4 fewer PPG. We’re projecting them as the 20th-best offense after this team led the league in scoring drives (49%) last season. __Daniel Jones__ is coming off a torn Achilles. __Alec Pierce__ is returning from ankle surgery. __Michael Pittman__ is gone. Their win total (7.5) is in the same bucket as the Panthers, Commanders, and Giants. This is all a concern for __Jonathan Taylor__ and his sensitivity to game-script. Taylor put up 31.5 FPG in wins but just 12.4 FPG in losses in 2025.

#### New Orleans Saints

__Tyler Shough__ is good. He was the best rookie QB last season, finishing QB11 in catchable throw rate and QB10 in completion rate over expectation. There is underrated rushing upside here, too. Shough averaged 2.3 designed carries per game, which was on par with __Drake Maye__ (2.4). Drafters should keep an open mind that this offense can find another gear in HC __Kellen Moore__’s second season. __Chris Olave__ was WR7 in expected FPG, WR8 in first-reads, and WR9 in target share. We’re projecting Olave’s volume to be strong again (WR9 in total targets).

#### Houston Texans

__C.J. Stroud__ averaged more EPA/DB than __Caleb Williams__ and __Bo Nix__ last season. Houston’s offense was by no means great, but they did finish 11th in scoring drives. Their defense is so good that it will give __David Montgomery__ plenty of good game-scripts to handle volume. Houston’s backfield was valuable in 2025; their RBs were just terrible. No backfield underperformed their expected FPG (-3.0) more than the Texans. This is an underrated team stack with Montgomery in Round 4, Stroud priced at QB23, and some cheap pass catchers late.

#### Washington Commanders

In the 20 career games that he’s played more than 85% of the snaps, Daniels averages 22.4 fantasy points per game. For reference, this would make him the QB2 behind only Josh Allen (22.6 FPG). He’s putting up +1.3 more FPG than Joe Burrow in this span, yet both players have nearly identical ADP. Daniels is averaging 52.1 rushing yards per start in his career, which basically ties Lamar Jackson (52 Rush YPG) over his last five seasons.

__Terry McLaurin__ is in line for career-best volume with a very thin depth chart behind him. In Daniels’ rookie season, 83% of McLaurin’s targets were catchable. That fell nine points to 74% last year. McLaurin was WR16 in 2024 by FPG, and he can get back to this level with a fully healthy Daniels. Washington’s defense is potentially bottom-5, which will lead to plenty of potential shootouts.

#### Minneapolis Vikings

The Vikings are 18th in projected FP and 20th in implied PPG. I really question __Kyler Murray__’s fit in this offense. Murray ranks QB36 in accurate throw rate and QB32 in CPOE on throws of 10+ yards out of 40 qualified passers over the last two seasons. As Jake Tribbey [noted](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/qb-positional-target-tendencies), Murray has been one of the league’s least efficient quarterbacks when he throws to his wide receivers. Minnesota’s backfield hasn’t been particularly valuable, ranking 25th, 17th, and 31st in PPR points scored over the last three years.

#### New York Giants

__Jaxson Dart__ with a healthy __Malik Nabers__ and __Andrew Thomas__ for 15-16 games would be really fun. Dart was around league-average in catchable and accurate throw rate without his best receiver, which is pretty good for a rookie. Dart was QB6 in FPG (20.7) across his 12 starts. Malik Nabers is WR6 by PPR FPG (17.4) all-time among WR in their first 2 seasons, trailing only Nacua (18.0), Jefferson (18.3), Chase (18.9), Randy Moss (19.0), and Odell Beckham (22.8).

__Bottom-10 Offenses__
----------------------

\> These are the worst offenses using a blend of projections and implied PPG.

Las Vegas Raiders – HC __Klint Kubiak__’s addition, along with __Fernando Mendoza__, brings fresh optimism. Getting T __Kolton Miller__ back healthy and adding __Tyler Linderbaum__ helps the offensive line outlook, too. The Raiders are the most likely offense to make the leap into the breakout or middle tier.

Pittsburgh Steelers – __Aaron Rodgers__ had the quickest time to throw and the lowest average depth of target among all passers last season. It’s really hard to run a passing offense this way.

Atlanta Falcons – __Bijan Robinson__ could lead all players in touches this season. The quality of the offense is the only concern.

Tennessee Titans – __Cam Ward__ flashed at times last season, but there is still a lot that needs to improve before this team can make a leap. The Titans have the 31st-ranked [offensive line](https://x.com/fball_insights/status/2074590563093893554?s=20). __Wan’Dale Robinson__ projects as a good-to-great value on DraftKings, as Jake Tribbey notes [here](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/qb-positional-target-tendencies#/).

Carolina Panthers – This offense will be without both starting tackles to start Week 1. Questions linger about __Bryce Young__. He ranks fourth-worst by passing yards per game (180.2) and second-worst by yards per pass attempt (6.0) among 52 QBs to have at least 1,000 pass attempts in their first 3 seasons since 2000. __Tetairoa McMillan__ is overvalued on Underdog (-4 spots behind ADP), but less so on DraftKings (ranked even with ADP).

Arizona Cardinals – The quality of the offense and potential for __Tyler Allgeier__ or __James Conner__ to steal goal-line work scares me off of __Jeremiyah Love__. The Cardinals are 32nd in implied PPG. I’m leaving the light on for __Marvin Harrison Jr.__ He only ended up playing in 9 full games last season due to injuries, but he quietly scored 13.4 PPR FPG (WR17). __Michael Wilson__ had a 12% target share and averaged 6.0 XFP/G with Harrison.

New York Jets – Speaking of which, __Breece Hall__ is projected for more FP than Love this season.

Miami Dolphins – __Malik Willis__ has averaged 58 rushing yards per game in 3 starts over the last two years. If he sustained that pace, it’d lead all QBs over Lamar Jackson (52) and Jayden Daniels (50). The rushing upside makes Willis a strong technical value.

Cleveland Browns – The Browns have the worst QB group (232 projected FP) and worst [offensive line](https://x.com/fball_insights/status/2074590563093893554?s=20) in football. It’s a huge concern for __Quinshon Judkins__’ outlook.

full_text:
Drafting the right players is the simplest way to win in fantasy football — we laid out the plan in our [2026 League-Winners, Targets, and Values](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/league-winners-targets-and-values#/) — but avoiding drafting the WRONG players is also critical. That’s why it’s important to understand which players we’re not so high on as a staff.

An __“OVERVALUE”__ is a player we don’t necessarily want to *avoid at all costs*, but his ADP makes him someone we’ll overlook unless it drops a little bit — we prefer other players at that specific cost.

An __“AVOID”__ is a player we’re almost certainly not drafting *at all* unless there’s a major market overcorrection.

What makes this article a little tougher than pointing out players we *do* want to draft is that there’s almost always a point where *every* player is worth drafting. However, the players in this article are those for whom such opportunities are scarce.

We broke this article down by position and ordered players by ADP. We’ll let you know if that player is overvalued or an avoid based on ADP, our projections, and any news and notes that have come out.

\> This article will be constantly updated throughout the preseason. ADP in this article is based on our [ADP tool’s PPR setting](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/rankings/adp), which pulls from NFFC drafts over the last 14 days.

 

{{CTA|FFPC|omit=\[none\]}}

__Quarterbacks__
----------------

#### OVERVALUE: __{{Joe Burrow|QB|CIN|21693}}__ (Cin)

\>ADP 57 QB4, PROJ QB6

We’re giving Burrow plenty of love in our projections this season, ranking him first in attempts, completions, and passing touchdowns, and third in passing yards. Even with his excellent passing game outlook, he still comes in sixth in FPG and sixth in FP in our projections because he doesn’t add a whole lot of value as a runner. Burrow is the only pass-heavy quarterback priced in the fifth to sixth round. In this tier, __Drake Maye__, __Jayden Daniels__, and __Jalen Hurts__ each have higher ceilings and higher floors than Burrow because of their rushing value. He should be drafted two to three rounds later than his current ADP in a tier with __Dak Prescott__, who we’re projecting for similar production but is being drafted in the eighth round or later. The only reason we’d be willing to spend up for Burrow at his current ADP is if we’re looking to build a stack with __Ja’Marr Chase__ or __Tee Higgins__ to raise the weekly ceilings for our teams. We recommend waiting a few rounds to select Prescott, __Matthew Stafford__, or __Jared Goff__ if you’re looking for better values among the pure pocket passers.

#### AVOID: __{{Patrick Mahomes|QB|KC|18890}}__ (KC)

\>ADP 100 QB12, PROJ QB13

The NFL gave it away that Mahomes was on track to be ready for Week 1 when they scheduled the Chiefs to host the Broncos on Monday Night Football. We received further confirmation when he participated during OTAs before avoiding the PUP list and being fully cleared to practice in training camp. He’ll be about nine months removed from ACL and LCL repairs at the start of the season after having surgery in mid-December for his Week 15 injury. It’s an awfully quick recovery for multiple ligament tears, and the Chiefs see no long-term issues with Mahomes after they signed him to a two-year extension, which will pay him $504.7 million through 2033.

Mahomes’ ADP has slowly begun to improve over the course of the summer, and it will continue to rise if it continues to look like he’ll be ready to play in Week 1. We’ll continue to avoid selecting him despite his QB4 (21.2 FPG) finish from last season, which was largely aided by career-highs in rushing TDs (5) and rushing YPG (30.1).
